summary.text: 远 means “far” or “distant.” It is the standardized simplified form of 遠, whose traditional graph combines 辵, a walking element, with 袁 as a sound element. An existing variant substituted 元 for 袁; this change was proposed because their readings sounded similar, though the original referent and pronunciation of 袁 remain unsettled.

formation.text: The traditional graph 遠 is analyzed as a phonosemantic compound: 辵 contributes the walking or road category, and 袁 supplies a sound cue. An earlier oracle-bone analysis identifies 彳 as the walking element alongside 袁. These accounts do not establish a precise graphic sequence between the forms. In 远, 元 replaces 袁 in an existing variant that was later standardized as the simplified form.

components.text: In 遠, 辵 contributes the walking or road category. An earlier oracle-bone analysis instead identifies 彳 in this role; the evidence does not establish a precise graphic sequence between them.
袁 is identified as the sound element in 遠. Its early graph has been interpreted as clothing with a hand or as someone putting clothing on; the depicted referent remains unsettled.

sound_limitation.text: The early 袁 graph’s referent and original pronunciation are unsettled. The readings below compare 袁 and 遠 but do not independently establish 袁’s identity or phonetic role; that role is supported by separate graph analyses.

sound.text: 袁 hjwon and 遠 hjwonX share the base form; X marks the host’s departing tone in this Middle Chinese notation.
The reconstructed forms are similar in the Baxter–Sagart system, consistent with the component analysis but not proof of it.
Modern Mandarin 袁 yuán and 遠 yuǎn have similar initials and finals but different tones; this present-day pairing alone does not establish the historical relation.

history.text: The selected oracle-script redraw illustrates the early analysis with 彳 and 袁; the seal-style redraw illustrates the traditional 辵 and 袁 analysis. They are modern renderings of different script styles, not evidence of a direct dated transition between the forms.

远 was used as a variant of 遠 with 元 substituted for 袁, and was later adopted as the standardized simplified form. The cited examples do not date individual specimens. A separate claim that 远 occurs in a dictionary compiled in 997 is not confirmed by the cited material.

uncertainties.text: The early form and referent of 袁 have competing interpretations; the depicted object’s name and original pronunciation are unsettled. This does not alter its documented analysis as the sound element in 遠.

Early evidence supports spatial distance, while later examples include kinship distance and figurative contexts. The evidence does not establish a dated path to “profound” or the verbal sense “keep away.”
The traditional component account is preserved in an early dictionary, but the available evidence does not settle every prehistoric detail of 遠’s formation.

senses.text: Oracle-bone examples use 遠 for spatial distance, including a hunting context that contrasts it with near. This is an early attested use, not necessarily the character’s hypothetical original meaning.
Warring States examples document 遠 in kinship contexts; the evidence does not date its development from spatial distance.

senses.period: Warring States texts; later lexicographic attestation also recorded
senses.text: Warring States examples include figurative contexts, and a later lexicographic record lists figurative depth. The evidence does not date a development from the spatial sense to this use.
A dictionary records a verbal use meaning “keep away,” but the evidence does not date it or connect it historically to the spatial sense.
Modern definitions include spatial distance and figurative depth; their chronology is not established here.

limitations.text: The early dated evidence establishes spatial distance. It does not establish priority among the other recorded senses or a semantic path connecting them.

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Variant Dictionary
evidence.text: The entry gives 遠 as “遼也。从辵，袁聲” and identifies 𨖸 as an ancient form. It records spatial and temporal distance, figurative depth, and kinship remoteness separately; it also records 遠去聲 for “keep away.” Its examples include the Shijing line “取彼斧斨，以伐遠揚” and the I Ching phrase “其旨遠.”
evidence.title: [A04172] 遠 — 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.field: 形義通解／甲骨、金文、戰國簡用例
evidence.text: The database analyzes oracle-bone 遠 as 彳 (road/walking semantic element) plus 袁 phonetic, and bronze 遠 as 辵 plus 袁 phonetic. It cites oracle-bone 《屯南》3759 contrasting 遠 and 邇 in a hunting context, bronze inscriptions on 晉姜鼎 and 番生簋蓋 referring to distant and near peoples, and Warring States bamboo texts using 遠 in distance, kinship, and figurative contexts. It describes the oracle-bone 袁 graph as an earlier graph later expanded with 彳 or 辵 for 遠; its account of the earliest 袁 graph and its referent includes competing interpretations, including a proposal that it depicts handling clothing. These are the database’s analyses, not independent confirmation of every graphic interpretation.

evidence.text: The database says oracle-bone 袁 forms include 衣 and 又, while noting an alternative interpretation that the graph depicts putting on clothing and may be an early form of 擐. The possible object or original referent depicted by 袁 remains uncertain; that uncertainty does not negate this source’s explicit analysis of 袁 as the sound element in 遠.

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Variant Dictionary
evidence.text: The dictionary classifies 远 as a variant of 遠 and says it appears in 《宋元以來俗字譜》 under 辵, citing popular novels. It explains the graphic substitution as changing the phonetic 袁 to 元. This supports treating 远 as a nonstandard variant later adopted as simplified form; the page does not itself date the cited novel examples individually.
evidence.title: [A04172] 遠 — 異體字研訂

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.text: The database reports 遠 meaning far in oracle-bone 《屯南》3759, in bronze inscriptions, and in Warring States bamboo texts. These provide distinct historical contexts for the spatial sense. Its cited early examples do not establish a dated development from distance to “profound,” social distance, or the verbal sense “keep away”; those senses are separately documented in later lexicographic examples rather than inferred here as a chronology.

evidence.field: 形義通解；甲骨、金文與戰國簡例
evidence.text: The database analyzes oracle-bone 遠 as 彳 (a road/walking element) plus phonetic 袁, and bronze forms as 辵 plus 袁. It gives 《屯南》3759 as an oracle-bone example contrasting 遠 and 邇 in a hunting context, cites bronze inscriptions using 遠 for distant peoples, and lists Warring States bamboo examples for spatial distance, kinship distance and figurative thought. The cited materials support an early spatial sense; they do not by themselves date a progression to every later sense.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 遠

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.text: The page quotes 說文: 遠，遼也。从辵，袁聲, and separately analyzes the earlier graph as 彳 plus phonetic 袁, with 彳 representing a road. This is historical lexicographic testimony and a modern database analysis, not independent proof of every prehistoric detail.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 遠

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.text: The source describes oracle-bone 袁 as forms containing 衣 and 又, usually interpreted as a hand holding clothing, while reporting 裘錫圭’s alternative that it depicts putting on clothing and may be an early graph of 擐. It says 袁 occurs for personal names and ‘distant place’ and that 遠 was made by adding 彳 or 辵 to 袁. The original referent and name/pronunciation of the depicted object are unsettled; the graph’s reported phonetic role in 遠 does not depend on identifying that object.

editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

The earliest cited attestation establishes spatial distance. The chronology linking spatial distance to profound/deep, social or kinship remoteness, and the verbal sense ‘keep away’ remains undemonstrated by dated examples in this research pass.

items.period: Shang oracle-bone script (as labeled by the Commons source family)
items.caption: This oracle-script form of 遠 combines a walking element with 袁, which serves as the phonetic element in the cited analysis.
items.alt: Black oracle-script glyph with a large curved walking element surrounding a central rounded form, and a separate upper stroke.
items.selection_reason: Shows the early graphic analysis relevant to the entry: the walking element marks the semantic component, while 袁 supplies the sound element.
items.rights: Public domain dedication for the vector representation, as stated on the Commons file page.

items.period: Seal-script style presented as Shuowen seal; conventional attribution to the late Zhou/Qin-Han scribal tradition is not independently dated by this file page
items.tradition: Shuowen seal-script style; modern vector redraw
items.caption: This seal-script rendering of 遠 illustrates the traditional analysis of the graph as 辵 with 袁 as its phonetic element.
items.alt: Black seal-script glyph with several vertically arranged strokes and a rounded enclosure, rendered in an elongated style.
items.selection_reason: Adds a useful comparison for the traditional 辵-plus-袁 analysis; it is a script-style rendering rather than evidence of a dated transition from the oracle form.
items.rights: Public domain representation, as stated on the Commons file page.

limitations.text: Both images are modern redrawings. The oracle image is labeled as oracle script, and the seal image is presented in Shuowen seal-script style; the exact date of the seal-style form is not established here.
The shape depicted by 袁 and its original referent remain disputed, although the cited analysis identifies 袁 as 遠’s phonetic element.
